## Foods & dishes
- [[World Wide Dishes]]: **47 dishes (39 Cameroon-only)**; free-text ingredients, no amounts or method, plus eating context (time of day, occasion, utensils, local-language name). Languages French 13, Hausa 6 and others; regions West 9, North 6. Examples: achu soup, njama njama, black soup, snail red soup, egusi pudding, fish roll. One of six countries with a 30-dish test set; **1,380 community image-review rows**.
- [[WorldCuisines]]: 8 dishes (5 Cameroon-only: achu, eru, ndolé, kwacoco, sangah); Wikipedia-style descriptions naming ingredients, no amounts.
- [[FmLAMA]]: 5 dishes (18 rows), e.g. ndolé, poulet DG, ikok, taro with yellow sauce; Wikidata ingredient lists, no amounts.

## Ingredients & food composition
- No national FCT is in the vault or `Backlog/`. The [[FAO INFOODS global databases]] candidate (priority 2, directory of 308 tables) is where a national or regional table would be found. Fallback: [[USDA FoodData Central]] by name matching. Cameroon is not in the ECOWAS table (WAFCT); a Central African table would have to come from the FAO/INFOODS directory.
- Plant occurrence: [[CMAUP]] 149 plants; [[NPASS]] 41 pairs (6 species, 40 compounds).

## Compounds & traditional medicine
- [[Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases|Duke]]: 25 ethnobotany records (19 taxa), mostly Ayensu.
- [[KNApSAcK Family]] lists Cameroon on its World map, but African flag pages were not scraped (counts unknown).
- Compound → effect chains come from the global backbone via [[Global]] ([[FooDB]], [[CTD]], [[Phenol-Explorer]], [[SpiceRx]], [[DDID]] for food–drug interactions).

## Gaps
- No Central African FCT and no recipes with amounts.
- Traditional medicine is nearly absent (25 Duke records) despite Cameroon's rich pharmacopoeia.
